issues.issue: Is petitioner a qualified individual (330-day physical presence + foreign tax home, abode not in US) entitled to the sec. 911(a)(1) exclusion of his Saudi wages?
issues.court: yes; exclusion up to the sec. 911(b)(2) limit (101,300 for 2016)
issues.diagnosis: Encoded with facts.foreign; the exclusion 101,300 (full-year 2016 cap; 109,024 exceeds it) matches. Qualification rests on findings: the 330-day count (credibility: Form 2555 25 days vs testimony 21 days, both < 35) and abode in Saudi Arabia (weighing of ties) - judgment inputs. Not modelled: no housing exclusion (employer compound, value not stated); wages for the ~21-25 US days treated as foreign earned income, as the court did.
issues.snippet: we conclude that petitioner's abode was in Saudi Arabia in 2016; therefore, he is entitled to exclude his foreign earned income up to the limitations

issues.issue: Tax on the remaining income (pension + wages over the limit) after the exclusion
issues.court: pension and wages over the limit taxable (amount under Rule 155)
issues.lean: 6891 (sec. 911(f) stacked regular tax 4,884 on TI 17,443 + sec. 72(t) 2,007)
issues.diagnosis: sec. 911(f) stacking now modelled: tax(17,443 + 101,300) - tax(101,300) = 4,884, plus 10% sec. 72(t) on the pension 2,007 = 6,891, equal to the hand computation. Court states the rule, not the amount (Rule 155). Caveat: sec. 72(t) kept as not conceded (age not stated).
issues.snippet: petitioner's pension income, along with the amount left over after accounting for limitations on his foreign earned income exclusion, both remain taxable

issues.lean: failureToFileApplies true; 1550 (25% x 6,891 = 1,723 less (c)(1) offset 2.5% x 6,891 = 172)
issues.diagnosis: Holding flag failureToFileApplies matches; liability rests on no reasonable cause shown (judgment input). Amount on the redetermined tax with the sec. 6651(c)(1) offset limited by (c)(2): 1,550, as hand-computed. No court amount (Rule 155).
issues.snippet: Petitioner does not argue, nor does the record show, that he had a meaningful defense to the imposition of the additions to tax.

issues.issue: Sec. 6651(a)(2) failure-to-pay addition on the SFR (sec. 6651(g)(2))
issues.lean: failureToPayApplies true; 1723 (25% x min(sfrTax 28,932, required 6,891), 50 months)
issues.diagnosis: Holding flag failureToPayApplies matches (SFR under sec. 6020(b), unpaid). sec. 6651(c)(2) applied: base is the redetermined 6,891, as the court ordered: 25% x 6,891 = 1,723. Liability rests on no reasonable cause shown (judgment input). No court amount (Rule 155).
issues.snippet: we sustain respondent's imposition of the additions to tax under section 6651(a)(1) and (2), with the "amount required to be shown as tax on [the] return" computed

issues.diagnosis: Wages 109,024 + pension 20,069 + COD 2,286 (later conceded), single, std ded 6,300 + exemption 4,050: TI 121,029, regular tax 26,925, plus 10% sec. 72(t) on the pension 2,007 = 28,932 exactly. Shows the notice included a 72(t) tax the opinion never mentions.
issues.snippet: respondent prepared a substitute for return pursuant to section 6020(b) for 2016 showing tax due of $28,932, plus additions to tax.

notes: Rerun 7175885f197 with facts.foreign (366 days, FEI 109,024) and sfrTax 28,932. Rule 155; no court amounts. Lean deficiency 6,891 (4,884 stacked regular + 2,007 sec. 72(t)); exclusion 101,300; FTF 1,550, FTP 1,723; holding flags match. Notice 28,932 reproduced exactly. Runner exit 0.
